title: QA test plan (orbit)
description: One feature's test plan as data, version 1. GENERATED by orbit from src/qa/{fields,vocab}.mjs — edit those, then `node cli/schema.mjs --write`. The Markdown beside it is rendered from this file; this one is the source. Shape lives here; the rules a shape cannot express live in src/qa/rules/.

$schema.description: Path to the plan schema, so the editor validates as you type.

schema.description: The metadata version this file is written to. 1 is what this engine reads.

id.description: Must equal the file name without .plan.json.

title.description: One line a human reads in a list of plans.

screen.description: The screen (an id in graph/screens.json) whose folder holds this plan: screens/<screen>/<id>.plan.json.

feature.description: The feature this plan is about, in the team's own words.

revision.description: This plan's own revision. Evidence recorded against an older one is history, not proof of this one.

at.description: When this revision was written (ISO date).

author.description: Who wrote it — a person to ask, not a signature.

scope.description: What this plan covers and what it deliberately does not.

sources.description: Where the expected behaviour came from, with a revision where one exists. A source that describes the IMPLEMENTATION is marked as such — it says what the code does, never what it should do.

map.description: The UI map and build this plan was designed against.

environments.description: Which environments this plan is meant to be run against. The project decides what the names mean.

budget.description: What there is room to run, so selection is a decision instead of an accident.

done.description: What has to be true for this plan to be finished. Written before the work, not after.

criteria.description: Acceptance criteria with stable IDs. Never invented: if nobody knows, it is an open question.

assumptions.description: What was taken as true without confirmation — each one a thing that can turn out wrong.

questions.description: What nobody could answer, linked to what it blocks. An assumed criterion produces a test that proves the assumption.

exclusions.description: Deliberately out of scope, with the reason. Shown in coverage — never silently dropped to flatter a ratio.

scenarios.description: The scenarios, each one derived with a technique.

manual.description: What no browser can observe, as checks a PERSON owns — never a JSON case that would quietly assert nothing.

note.description: Anything a reader of this plan needs that no field above holds.

out.description: What is not, so a reader does not assume it was.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. REQ1 — criteria cite it.

kind.description: What kind of source. `code` and `commit` describe the IMPLEMENTATION: they say what the product does, which is not evidence of what it should do.

ref.description: Where to find it — an id, a url, a path.

revision.description: Which revision was read. Without one, nothing can say whether it has moved since.

says.description: What it says, quoted or summarised.

authority.description: Whether this is the team's ACCEPTED requirement or still a draft. Absent reads accepted in a committed plan and draft in an agent's draft plan; a criterion from a draft source prepares tests and never confirms a finding.

digest.description: The digest of what was read, so a source that moved with no new revision is noticed rather than trusted.

dialect.description: The dialect a contract document is written in -- e.g. openapi-3.1, asyncapi-3.0, json-schema/2020-12 -- so a reader of it is chosen by what it is, never guessed.

fe_commit.description: The frontend commit the map was at when this plan was designed.

captured.description: When the map was last confirmed against the running app.

minutes.description: How many minutes of running there is room for.

profile.description: Which set this budget is for — a name the team uses, such as smoke or release.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. AC1. Quoted in tickets and commits, so it never changes meaning.

says.description: The criterion, in the words of whoever owns the feature.

source.description: Which source id it came from.

risk.description: What it would cost to get this wrong.

disposition.description: Only when no scenario covers it: why not, and what happens instead.

expects.description: What the criterion states as STRUCTURED expectations over observed meanings. Only these can be mapped to an assertion without anybody's judgement; prose still prepares a test, and never confirms one.

about.description: The system graph node it is about, by its logical alias (a node's name, lower-case, every other character a dash).

obligations.description: Which kinds of property it states, as obligation shapes (src/qa/obligations/shapes.mjs). Only these are derived into test obligations; none is guessed from the prose.

property.description: The observed meaning it is about, e.g. response.status, effect.count, message.id -- never a provider's field name.

op.description: What must hold of it (src/qa/vocab.mjs EXPECT_OPS).

value.description: The value the criterion states: a number, a word, a list -- exactly as its owner wrote it.

within.description: The window, in seconds, an absence or a completion is claimed within. Required for those two; never invented.

for.description: Which of the criterion's obligations this expectation states, by shape. Absent: every one whose shape rules with its op. Empty: none -- a slot a design may still rule an auxiliary step with (a barrier, a positive control).

because.description: Where in the source it says so.

state.description: Why this criterion has no scenario. `open` means it is not decided yet — which is a gap, said out loud.

because.description: The reason. A disposition with no reason is a criterion quietly dropped.
Why it was reasonable to assume it.

asks.description: The question, as it would be put to the person who knows.

blocks.description: The criteria and scenarios this question holds up.

owner.description: Who can answer it. `unassigned` when nobody has been asked yet.

state.description: Answered means the answer is in the plan, not in somebody's memory.

answer.description: What they said, once they said it.

because.description: Why. Shown in the coverage report beside what was covered.

technique.description: The technique this exclusion decides against -- a security obligation the plan derived (permission, scoping) is then answered, not owed.

impact.description: How bad it is for the business if this is wrong.

likelihood.description: How likely it is to be wrong.

usage.description: How often this path is actually used.

blast.description: How much of the change touches it.

history.description: How often this area has broken before.

because.description: Why these numbers. A score with no sentence is a number nobody can argue with.

as.description: The logical identity that performs it — a kind of user, never a profile name.

notRoles.description: Roles this actor must NOT hold. This says who is RUNNING; it is not, by itself, evidence the product refused anything.

owner.description: Who owns the resource being acted on — the actor, or somebody else.

tenant.description: Which tenant the resource belongs to.

state.description: The business state the resource is in when the action starts.

need.description: required = this layer must rule on it · n-a = it does not apply · unverifiable = it applies and nothing here can check it. The third is a capability gap, never a lowered bar.

says.description: The expected result on this layer, concretely enough to be checked.

because.description: Why it does not apply, or what is missing. Required for anything but `required`.

lacks.description: The permission this actor does NOT have — the thing being tested.

ui.description: What the screen must do: the control is hidden, disabled, or the attempt shows an error. Required — a permission scenario with no observable refusal proves nothing.

backend.description: What the server must do, when there is a way to drive the attempt past the UI. `unverifiable` with a reason is an honest answer; silence is not.

unchanged.description: The evidence that nothing changed when the attempt was refused.

because.description: Why this combination is the one worth testing.

kind.description: How the action happens a second time. `concurrent` means at the same moment — a sequence described as concurrency tests nothing about racing.

expect.description: What the CONTRACT says the second attempt produces. Not assumed: a second create is not automatically a duplicate, nor automatically the same status.

extra.description: What must NOT appear — the second row, the second message, the second charge.

guarded.description: true when the linked case's skip-if guard is there to protect a re-RUN. It protects the run; it is not evidence about the product.

kind.description: What this scenario changes. Not only create: an update that writes the wrong row is the same class of bug.

after.description: The state after — what must be true of the data, not of the screen.

unchanged.description: What must have stayed exactly as it was. The half people forget, and where scoping bugs are caught.

onRefusal.description: What must be true when the action is refused or fails part way.

effect.description: The "<screen>/<via>" the map already traced for this action, so the plan cites the map instead of re-typing it.

data.description: per-run = made fresh and identifiable · fixture = deliberately seeded and shared · existing = whatever is there, which is how order-dependence starts.

key.description: The business key that identifies this scenario's own data, e.g. a TC- prefixed name.

record.description: How the record id is obtained when the key is not enough.

scope.description: Which owner or tenant the data belongs to.

cleanup.description: How it is put back. SQL verification is read-only here, so cleanup is a UI action, a fixture reset, or a person — never a written statement.

onFailure.description: What is left behind when the scenario stops half way, and who deals with it.

isolation.description: How this avoids depending on the order the scenarios run in.

accepted.description: What the product may legitimately answer immediately — an acknowledgement is not a result.

complete.description: The business condition that means it actually finished.

deadline.description: How many seconds completion is allowed to take.

because.description: Where that deadline came from. A number with no source is a guess that will be tuned until the test goes green.

observe.description: Which layers are actually watched for completion (ui, api, sql). A reload is not a commit, so the screen alone does not settle it.

unverified.description: The part of the flow nothing here can see.

kind.description: What kind of thing is in the way. `map` and `capability` block AUTOMATION — they are not a reason to drop the scenario from the plan.

says.description: What is missing, and what would unblock it.

id.description: The case id, found in whichever ui-tests/screens/<screen>/cases/ holds it. One scenario may have several; one case may serve several scenarios.

state.description: How far the case has got. Claimed here and CHECKED against the file — a link claiming `validated` about a case that does not validate is a finding.

covers.description: Which part of the scenario this case covers, when it does not cover all of it.

because.description: What that is based on — a past run, a similar case. Without a basis it is a wish.

name.description: One line: what this scenario does.

covers.description: Which criteria (and other scenarios' risks) this covers. Coverage is this list — never guessed from a case name.

technique.description: How this scenario was derived. Some techniques oblige a block: permission asks for `denial`, idempotency for `repeat`.

why.description: Why it is worth the time. The answer that is not 'for completeness'.

priority.description: P1 the feature is broken without it · P2 real but survivable · P3 nice to have.

must.description: true when this one runs in every profile. A must that does not fit the budget is a reported shortfall, never a quiet demotion.

profiles.description: Which named sets this belongs to — smoke, regression, release, whatever the team calls them.

because.description: Why this priority, when the risk numbers would suggest another.

risk.description: The factors behind the priority. Only the ones there is evidence for.

actor.description: Who performs it, what they hold, and whose data they touch.

preconditions.description: What must already be true before the first step.

data.description: Where this scenario's data comes from and what happens to it.

intent.description: What the steps DO, in intent — never selectors. The case writer turns these into edges.

expect.description: The expected result per layer (ui, api, sql). Every layer says required, n-a or unverifiable, with a reason — silence about a layer is how a case ends up proving less than it claims.

mutation.description: What changes, what must not, and what happens when it is refused.

repeat.description: What happens when the action is performed a second time, or twice at once.

async.description: For anything that finishes after the response: what is accepted, what counts as done, and how long it may take.

denial.description: For a permission or scoping scenario: who is refused, and how the refusal is OBSERVED.

dependsOn.description: Scenario ids that must run first. A cycle here is a finding, not an ordering.

blockers.description: What stops it today. A blocker is a reason it cannot be automated yet, not a reason to leave it out of the plan.

execution.description: auto = a JSON case · manual = a person · mixed = both, and the plan says which part is which.

checks.description: The manual check ids that cover the rest of it.

estimate.description: How long it takes, when there is something to base that on.

readiness.description: The DESIGN state only: is enough known to write this. Not whether a case exists, and not whether it passed.

name.description: One line: what a person checks.

covers.description: The criteria and scenarios this check covers.

because.description: Why it is not automated — a queue, a mail, a scheduled job, a thing no browser can see.

owner.description: The person or team who does it. `unassigned` when nobody has been asked — which is honest, and visible.

preconditions.description: What must be true before they start.

expect.description: What they must see. A check with no expected result cannot be passed or failed.

evidence.description: What they capture, so somebody else can believe the answer.

state.description: Where this check is. `done` is a claim about a person's work and needs its evidence.
